moat_against: No true pricing power — Medicare/Medicaid administered rates, commercial rates negotiated vs large payers
Payer-mix/policy hostage: exchange and Medicaid enrollment shifts already hurting volumes and mix
Labor is the largest cost line; post-pandemic cost normalization can reverse
HCA larger in hospitals; Optum/SCA and physician de novos contest ASC growth
Levered balance sheet limits flexibility in a downturn
moat_for: USPI largest ASC operator (538 facilities vs SCA Health 320) with 11,000+ affiliated physicians
Health-system JV partnerships (Baylor Scott & White, Memorial Hermann) feeding acquisition pipeline
Scale in payer contracting, supply chain and scheduling across hospitals and ASCs
Licensed local hospital assets with high-acuity service lines hard to enter against
Conifer revenue-cycle scale, wholly owned again after CommonSpirit buyback
moat_justification: USPI's scale as the largest ASC platform (538 facilities vs next-largest 320) plus licensed local hospital assets and payer/supply-chain scale give a moderate moat, but pricing is payer-administered/negotiated, the model is labor- and capex-heavy, ASCs are contestable by Optum/SCA, HCA and physician de novos, and payer-mix/policy risk is live.
name: Tenet Healthcare Corporation
one_liner: Transformed hospital/USPI operator, moat 5/10 — clears 15% only marginally on a windfall-normalized TTM base (weighted IRR 15.2%, IV@15 $257 vs $254 price) while the median-base method is Tier C; size like a borderline B/C, and $257 is the 15%-clearing price with no margin of safety.
